Q: How can I run a Flutter application in a Flatpaked Chromium browser in Android Studio? A:

We can work around the required executable by creating a shell skript

#!/usr/bin/env bash
flatpak run io.github.ungoogled_software.ungoogled_chromium "$@"

Create it at a location useful to you, and then make it executable. I named it "chromium". Then set the env var to the location of the script

chmod +x chromium
export CHROME_EXECUTABLE="/my/path/to/chromium"

After running flutter doctor again, it should pick it up.

> flutter doctor
Doctor summary (to see all details, run flutter doctor -v):
[✓] Flutter (Channel stable, 3.41.4, on Arch Linux 6.19.8-arch1-1, locale en_US.UTF-8)
[✓] Android toolchain - develop for Android devices (Android SDK version 36.1.0)
[✓] Chrome - develop for the web
[✗] Linux toolchain - develop for Linux desktop
    ✗ CMake is required for Linux development.
      It is likely available from your distribution (e.g.: apt install cmake), or can be downloaded from https://cmake.org/download/
[✓] Connected device (2 available)
[✓] Network resources

! Doctor found issues in 1 category.

Now we need to make the env var persistent. Depending on how you launch Android Studio, there are different ways. If you launch it via your start menu (meaning over a .desktop file), you can simply add the following line to ~/.local/share/applications/android-studio.desktop

Exec=env CHROME_EXECUTABLE=/my/path/to/chromium android-studio %f

After closing Android Studio and restarting it over the start menu, the "Chrome (web)" config appears in the top right corner.

Q: Median for data between 2 dates A:

If you wanted to split the data by months, you could use Groupby:

=GROUPBY(IFERROR(MONTH(A1:A7),"Month"),B1:B7,MEDIAN,3,0)
Date Value
01/01/2026 1 Month Value
02/01/2026 2 1 2
03/01/2026 3 2 5
01/02/2026 4
02/02/2026 5
03/02/2026 6

Where my dates are DD/MM/YY.

Q: How do I create a homebrew tap in the same tree as my source? A:

homebrew tap is expected to have a name with prefix homebrew- by default, so you must pass the repo url if it doesn't have the prefix. To build bottle, it is better to start with

brew tap-new <git-username>/homebrew-tap

and then you could copy github action scripts from this brand new tap.
